newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods sink amid another NYMEX selloff.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods sink amid another NYMEX selloff.

text.p: Prices of U.S. spot refined products followed NYMEX futures sharply lower late Friday, repeating Thursday's downhill performance although some of the pain was offset by firmer differentials on Gulf Coast distillates, players said.

Diffs on USG heating oil improved to 1.20 cents below the March print for front-fourth-cycle material, about 0.60 cent stronger than Thursday diffs, players said, attributing the gain to short-covering.

"A lot of traders, including some Wall Street types, are short and had to cover," one Gulf player said, noting there was little other market direction and afternoon activity was slow ahead of the weekend.
March NYMEX heating oil futures settled 0.92 cent lower on the heels of a 1.87 cent decline seen Thursday in a selloff led by crude oil.
New York Harbor heat diffs were stable at about 1.75 cents over the screen late Friday, with sellers hiding out a second day in a row amid the tumbling NYMEX values, traders said.
Front-fourth-cycle USG low sulfur diesel was sold for 0.75 cent above the print, with diffs rebounding from Thursday's half-cent differential loss.
